Every process after the current one in self.processes is then never waited on or terminated. For example, with 3 flusher processes and a short timeout, if process 0 uses up the budget, processes 1 and 2 are left running.

judge_pairs.reason: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is always false for SpawnProcess, so hung flusher processes are never killed.

comment_verdicts.text:
AssignmentSource.queued default is evaluated once at import time
The dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls `timezone.now()` once, when the module is imported. `from_integration` never passes `queued`, so every AssignmentSource built in a long-running worker or web process gets the same stale timestamp, which is the process start time. `to_dict()` then serializes that stale value into the task kwargs.
The `queued` value does not show when the assignment was queued. Any later logic or debugging that relies on it sees a wrong time, and it can be hours or days old.

judge_pairs.reason: Dataclass field default timezone.now() is evaluated once at import, giving a shared stale default timestamp for queued.

CreateOrUpdateDevice counts devices and then inserts in a separate statement. Concurrent requests from different new devices can all read count < limit and all insert.
